chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The servant may be oppressed, so he does not cease to supplicate (against his oppressor) until he becomes unjust.'

key_terms.ظَالِماً: Unjust (one who commits injustice or is deemed unjust by God due to excessive du'a)

ai.seo_question: How can an oppressed person become unjust through supplication?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual danger of lingering resentment, where the oppressed individual, through persistent supplication for retribution, may transition from being a victim to becoming an oppressor (*zhaliman*) by accumulating divine favor that alters their spiritual status. Scholars interpret this not merely as becoming unjust in action, but as the soul becoming hardened or entitled, potentially leading to a state where their own merits are weighed against their lingering grievances. This serves as a cautionary principle for believers to balance their du'a with patience (*sabr*) and justice (*adl*) to avoid the subtle corruption of the self.
